findings.note: Spec 5 omits the judge-override knobs that ship on this branch, including in its security-critical closed env-name set. internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:31-32 defines EnvJudgeModel=METAREVIEW_JUDGE_MODEL and EnvJudgeEffort=METAREVIEW_JUDGE_EFFORT, and internal/fsm/cli/run.go:113 parses --judge-model/--judge-effort. The spec's section 6 (lines 356-358) states 'the closed set of env names the binary reads' and lists only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_BASE_URL, MOCK_AI, MRV_RUN_ID, HOME plus test-only names; both METAREVIEW_JUDGE_* are missing, so the closed-set claim is false against the code it specifies. The same omission runs through section 2's 'final' grammar (lines 55-56, 60: init/advance carry no --judge-model/--judge-effort) and section 4's required --agent-prompt content (lines 242-244), even though the shipped golden testdata/fsm/agent-prompt.golden:36 and skills/fsm/SKILL.md:81-82 both name them. The shipped docs are correct; the spec that is supposed to be their authority is stale, which is exactly the class of defect the head commit (334e752, 'the claims that disagreed with the code') was addressing. Fix by adding the flags to section 2, the knob sentence to section 4, and the two env names to section 6's closed set.

findings.note: The Codex CLI judge provider is missing from spec 5's seams and its proxy claim does not hold for it. Section 2 line 64 already assumes codex models ('a codex/ model also takes none|minimal|max'), but section 8's Deps block (lines 430-446) has neither the CodexExec seam nor the After seam that internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:34 and :40 actually declare, and section 8's wiring sentence (line 449) names judge.New(HTTP, Keys, URLs, nonce, Clock) where internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:144-146 calls judge.NewWithCodex(..., c.deps.CodexExec). Section 8 claims 'tested at 100% with fakes for every seam', which cannot be verified against a Deps list that is missing two seams. More materially, section 6 line 359 asserts 'no proxy variables - RealDeps clones http.DefaultTransport with Proxy = nil'; that justification covers only the HTTP arm. internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:97-107 (realCodexExec) sets no cmd.Env, so a codex/ judge inherits the entire parent environment - HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and both API keys included - into a third-party binary, and section 6's own child-env containment rule at line 354 ({PATH,HOME,LANG,TMPDIR} intersect the declared set) is written as if cmd children were the only spawns. skills/fsm/SKILL.md:76-80 documents the codex spawn and that it sits outside the allowed_cmds consent gate; spec 5 records none of it, and section 5's black-box inventory has no codex or judge-override row (tests/go/test-fsm.sh has zero matches for judge-model). Fix by adding CodexExec/After to the Deps block, correcting the wiring call, qualifying the proxy sentence for the inherited-env subprocess, and adding the codex arm to the section 5 inventory.

findings.note: Section 3's exit-code authority misdescribes the function it names. Lines 166-168 declare 'cli.exitFor(command, phase, code) with phase in open|advance|fork|record|judge'; the implementation at internal/fsm/cli/envelope.go:67 is exitFor(code string, ph phase, repairMoved bool) - no command parameter at all - and its phase vocabulary at envelope.go:46-48 includes two phases the spec never lists, phaseInit and phaseNone, both of which carry real routing (ERR_STORE_PATH and ERR_RUNS_JSONL branch on init; phaseNone returns 2 unconditionally for run-less commands and judge without --run). Since the spec calls this table 'the sole authority', its phase set has to be the complete one, and a table keyed on a command argument the function does not receive cannot be implemented as written. The same signature is repeated in the ledger at line 502.

evidence.note: Declares exitFor(command, phase, code) with a five-value phase set.

findings.note: Internal contradiction in the test-coverage commitment for the exit table. Section 3 line 168 and section 5 line 317 both require 'one row per (command, phase, code) triple'; section 8's Tests paragraph at line 480 requires 'one row per (command, code) pair of the exit table'. The two are different obligations - the pair form drops the phase distinction that the table's whole design rests on (ERR_GIT, ERR_CMD_CHANGED, ERR_RUN_TERMINAL, ERR_RUN_LOCKED and ERR_STORE_PATH all split 2-vs-1 by phase) - so an implementer following section 8 would under-test exactly the rows the table exists to pin. Pick the triple form in all three places.

evidence.note: Section 8: 'one row per (command, code) pair of the exit table'.
Section 5: 'one row per (command, phase, code) triple of the exit table'.
Section 3 also says triple, making section 8 the odd one out.
